q: The compounds formed by the combination of two elements are called _____ compounds.
e: The compounds formed by the combination of two elements are called binary compounds.

q: The compounds formed by the combination of three elements are called _____ compounds.
e: The compounds formed by the combination of three elements are called ternary compounds.

q: A heterogeneous mixture is one that is non-uniform, and where the different components of the mixture can be _____.
e: A heterogeneous mixture is one that is non-uniform, and where the different components of the mixture can be seen.

q: A homogeneous mixture is one in which the composition of its components are _____ mixed throughout.
e: A homogeneous mixture is one in which the composition of its components are uniformly mixed throughout.

q: An alloy is a substance made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to _____.
e: An alloy is made by combining metallic elements to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

q: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is _____ in nature.
e: Magnetic separation is used when at least one component is magnetic in nature.

 ), sugar and common salt are _____ in water.
e: Some solids such as copper(II) sulphate, sugar and common salt are soluble in water.

q: Some solids such as sand, charcoal and chalk are _____ in water.
e: Some solids such as sand, charcoal and chalk are insoluble in water.

q: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions and are called _____ liquids.
e: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions and are called miscible liquids.

q: Liquids that do not mix are called _____ liquids.
e: Liquids that do not mix are called immiscible liquids.

q: Dry air is a familiar example of a _____ solution.
e: Dry air is a familiar example of a gaseous solution.

q: Brass is an example of a _____ solution.
e: Brass (copper and zinc) is an example of a solid solution.

q: Salt water is a familiar example of a solid dissolved within a _____.
e: Salt water is a familiar example of a solid dissolved within a liquid.

q: Carbonated water contains carbon dioxide gas molecules existing between molecules of _____.
e: Carbonated water contains carbon dioxide gas molecules existing between molecules of water.

q: Blood and saliva are some of the more familiar solutions of _____ importance.
e: Blood and saliva are some of the more familiar solutions of biological importance.

q: A solution is a _____ mixture of two or more substances.
e: A solution is a homogeneous (uniform) mixture of two or more substances.

q: When sugar is mixed with water, the sugar is the _____ and water is the solvent.
e: When you mix sugar with water, the sugar is the solute, and water is the solvent.

q: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as _____ solutions.
e: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as aqueous solutions.

q: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an _____ solution.
e: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an unsaturated solution.

q: A _____ solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred.
e: A saturated solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature.

q: The amount in grams of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the _____ of that solute.
e: The amount (in grams) of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the solubility.

q: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a _____ solution.
e: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a supersaturated solution.

q: When the temperature of the solution is increased, the solubility of most solutes _____.
e: When the temperature of the solution is increased the solubility of the solute increases.

q: The solubility of all gases and some solids such as calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate _____ when temperature of the solution is increased.
e: The solubility of all gases and some solids such as calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate decreases when temperature of the solution is increased.

q: In a solution, the solute is _____ distributed throughout the solution.
e: In a solution the solute is uniformly distributed throughout the solution.

q: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a _____ mixture.
e: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a homogeneous mixture.

q: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's _____.
e: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's crust.

q: Nutrients are carried in water solution to all parts of a _____.
e: Nutrients are carried in water solution to all parts of a plant.

q: Ethanol, acetic acid and sulphuric acid are _____ in water.
e: Ethanol, acetic acid and sulphuric acid are soluble in water.

q: Petrol and oils are _____ in water.
e: Petrol and oils are insoluble in water.

q: Hydrogen chloride and ammonia are gases that are _____ in water.
e: Some gases such as hydrogen chloride and ammonia are soluble in water.

q: Oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are gases that are not very _____ in water.
e: Some gases such as oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are not very soluble in water.

q: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate _____ g of water, at that temperature.
e: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate 100 g of water, at that temperature.

q: A solution in which more of the solute can dissolve at the given temperature is called an _____ solution.
e: A solution in which more of the solute can dissolve at the given temperature is called unsaturated solution.

q: The solution that retains more solute than that required to saturate the solution at room temperature is called a _____ solution.
e: The solution that retains more solute than that required to saturate the solution at room temperature is called a supersaturated solution.

q: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility decreases, so the excess solute will come out as a _____.
e: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility decreases, so the excess solute will come out as solid.

q: Wine is separated from the sediments by _____ in daily life applications.
e: Wine is separated from the sediments by decantation.

q: Plasma can be removed from blood by decantation after _____.
e: Plasma can be removed from blood by decantation after centrifugation.

q: Milk is a colloid of fat globules suspended in water, which is an example of a _____ mixture.
e: Colloidal mixtures (heterogeneous) have components that tend not to settle out, such as milk.

q: Decanting a mixture containing flammable solvents can be dangerous as the flammable material evaporates and forms dangerous _____.
e: Decanting a mixture containing flammable solvents can be dangerous as the flammable material evaporates and forms dangerous fumes.
